name: Brain
what_it_does: Controls thinking, memory, attention and sleep.
what_space_does: Crews sleep about 6 hours with 8.5 hours scheduled. High CO₂ is linked to headaches. Fatigue slows attention.
what_affects_it_on_earth: After landing: tiredness and readjusting routines.
how_to_care: Keep a regular sleep time; log headaches; report high CO₂.
eva_focus: Sleep the night before, dizziness, fatigue before and during the spacewalk.
nasa_risks: Sleep, circadian and workload risk|CO2 Risk|Team Risk|Behavioral Health Risk (context only: NASA tracks it, but Maia does not monitor mood or mental health in v2)
evidence_level: consensus (risks, sleep data); NEEDS VALIDATION (what_it_does wording)

name: Eyes
what_it_does: Focus light so you can see clearly.
what_space_does: The headward fluid shift is the leading hypothesis for SANS: optic disc edema, globe flattening and hyperopic shift; some changes persist after flight.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Vision changes may last after return. Dust and bright light can irritate the eyes.
how_to_care: Do the weekly vision check. Report blurred vision or wavy lines.
eva_focus: Visor fog or glare; dust on the Moon.
nasa_risks: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS Risk)|Dust Risk

name: Ears
what_it_does: Hear sounds and keep your balance.
what_space_does: The balance system re-adapts on arrival and on return. Constant cabin noise can affect hearing.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Dizziness and unsteady walking in the first days after landing.
how_to_care: Report dizziness or ringing in the ears. Use hearing protection where advised.
nasa_risks: Sensorimotor Risk|Risk of Hearing Loss and Performance Decrements Due to Acoustics Issues in Space

name: Heart
what_it_does: Pumps blood with oxygen to the whole body.
what_space_does: About 2 L of fluid shifts toward the head; 24-h blood pressure falls ~8–10 mmHg in long flights. After return, pressure can drop when standing.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Fainting or dizziness when standing up after landing. On Earth: high blood pressure, inactivity.
how_to_care: Aerobic exercise, enough fluids, stand up slowly after landing.
eva_focus: Workload and heat; a pulse above 140 bpm marks impairment.
nasa_risks: Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations Contributing to Adverse Mission Performance and Health Outcomes (CV Risk)|Concern of Venous Thromboembolism|Risk of Reduced Physical Performance Capabilities Due to Reduced Aerobic Capacity (Aerobic Risk)

name: Lungs
what_it_does: Bring oxygen into the blood and remove CO₂.
what_space_does: Lungs work normally, but cabin air quality matters: high CO₂ causes headache; dust on the Moon can irritate airways.
what_affects_it_on_earth: On Earth: asthma, COPD, smoke and air pollution.
how_to_care: Report high CO₂ or smells. Keep the cabin air checked.
eva_focus: Inspired CO₂ in the helmet (suit status ring).
nasa_risks: Risk of Reduced Crew Health and Performance Due to Hypoxia|CO2 Risk|Dust Risk|Risk of Toxic Substance Exposure

name: Bones
what_it_does: Hold up your body and store calcium.
what_space_does: Weight-bearing bones lose about 1–1.5% of their mineral each month.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Higher fracture risk after return. On Earth: inactivity and ageing.
how_to_care: Resistance exercise every day; calcium and vitamin D as advised.
eva_focus: Shoulder, hand and joint pain; deep joint pain after EVA can be decompression sickness.
nasa_risks: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone|Risk of In-Mission Injury and Performance Decrements and Long-term Health Effects due to Dynamic Loads (Dynamic Loads Risk)|Risk of Mission Impacts and Long-Term Health Issues due to Decompression Sickness

name: Muscles
what_it_does: Move your body and keep you strong.
what_space_does: Muscles shrink and fitness drops without load.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Weakness after return. On Earth: inactivity.
eva_focus: Forearm and hand fatigue from the gloves.
nasa_risks: Risk of Reduced Physical Performance Capabilities Due to Reduced Muscle Size, Strength, and Endurance (Muscle Risk)|Risk of Mission Impacting Injury and Compromised Performance and Long-Term Health Effects due to EVA Operations (EVA Risk)

name: Kidneys
what_it_does: Clean the blood and balance water and salts.
what_space_does: More calcium in the urine raises the risk of kidney stones; emptying the bladder can be harder.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Dehydration in heat. On Earth: not drinking enough.
how_to_care: Drink to your water target; follow the diet advice.
eva_focus: Water: 950 mL drink bag; 240 mL per suited hour.
nasa_risks: Risk of Renal Stone Formation|Risk of Urinary Retention|Food and Nutrition Risk

name: Skin
what_it_does: Protects the body and helps control temperature.
what_space_does: Rashes and small skin problems are among the most expected minor conditions.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Sun and cold exposure. On Earth: small wounds that heal slowly.
how_to_care: Keep skin clean and dry; report rashes or wounds.
nasa_risks: Non-Ionizing Radiation Risk|Risk of Mission Impacting Injury and Compromised Performance and Long-Term Health Effects due to EVA Operations (EVA Risk)

name: Immune system
what_space_does: Stress can wake up dormant viruses; the immune response changes. Radiation adds long-term cancer risk.
what_affects_it_on_earth: Infections after return. On Earth: poor sleep and stress lower defences.
how_to_care: Sleep, hygiene, report fever or new symptoms.
nasa_risks: Risk of In Mission Impacts, Adverse Health Events or Long-Term Health Impacts due to Altered Immune Response (Immune Risk)|Risk of Adverse Health Effects Due to Host-Microorganism Interactions|Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis
